title: Does Hot Water Really Freeze Faster?

fin.big: Simplified illustrations. The case is still disputed.
fin.small: Sources: Burridge & Linden, Scientific Reports 6:37665 (2016); Jeng, American Journal of Physics 74:514 (2006); Mpemba & Osborne, Physics Education 4:172 (1969)

parts: Hot water or cold water. Which one freezes first?
Stay to the end. The answer may hide in one centimeter.
In the nineteen sixties, a Tanzanian schoolboy was making ice cream.
Short on freezer space, he put his mix in still boiling.
A classmate's cooler mix went in too.
Ninety minutes later, his had frozen. The other had not.
His name: Erasto Mpemba. The puzzle is named after him.
Aristotle wrote about it too. But the real twist is the thermometer.
In twenty sixteen, two scientists in England tested water with great care.
No evidence of a real head start for hot water.
The catch? Misplace the thermometer by one centimeter, and the data can mimic the effect.
Others say the real test is full freezing. The case stays open.
Our reading: don't bet your ice cubes on it. Next: why purple was for kings.
